newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker in heavy trading.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker in heavy trading.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks ended weaker in heavy trading on Tuesday * Banks and consumer products led five of 14 sub-groups lower * 108.9 million shares traded for a value of C$1.44 billion
Toronto stocks finished weaker in heavy trading on Tuesday, depressed by weak bonds and modest profit-taking, traders said.
The TSE 300 Composite Index slipped 4.98 points to 5436.54 in brisk turnover of 108.9 million shares worth C$1.44 billion.
Declining stocks outnumbered advances 500 to 454 with 253 issues ending flat.
The TSE, Canada's biggest stock market, has enjoyed a strong rally in recent weeks, setting an all-time high of 5441.50 on Monday.
In today's action, banking and consumer products led five of 14 sub-groups into negative territory. Conglomerates and precious metals led the strong side.
Investors took profits from Canadian bank stocks which have soared to new heights in recent weeks, traders said.
Canada's bond market also turned in a weak performance which spilled into equities. Canada's 9.00 percent long bond dropped 0.45 to 106.15 to yield 7.464 percent.
The TSE fell in sympathy with Wall Street where the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 13 points.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Shell Canada Ltd jumped 1.80 to 45.95 after announcing plans to sell its chemicals division to a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell group for C$635 million.
* PC DOCS Group International Inc led net losers, falling 5.30 to close at 11.60 after warning its first quarter results will be below analysts' expectations.
* Toronto Dominion Bank topped the most-active list, easing 0.20 to 29.75 on 2.8 million shares. Royal Bank of Canada surrendered 0.50 to 40.80 on 1.27 million shares.
* Molson Cos jumped 0.90 to 20.55 on 1.08 million shares after an analyst issued a buy recommendation for the brewer.
